messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a riend
Shubham Vyas it is
shubham vyas... solid name. where you working these days?
bp (British Petroleum)
bp... that's the big oil play, global energy transitions and all that. found you on linkedin - shubham bhartee, data steward at bp. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/shubham-bhartee-321b90166
No that's not me, search vai, "Shubham Vyas"
better! found shubham vyas - software engineer ii at bp, ex-amazon. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/shubham-vyas-a9482018a
Yes you got me!

amazon to bp... that's an interesting pivot from tech giant to energy infrastructure. building software for oil and gas operations hits different than aws. what made you jump from bezos land to big oil?

Better opportunity, to build something from scratch for bp which is not much ahead in terms of software and tooling like Amazon is. 
Amazon is amazing place but to expand learning I needed to come out of amazonified ecosystem.

smart move. amazon's great for learning scale but once you're in that ecosystem, everything feels... amazonified. bp probably feels like the wild west compared to aws's polished machine. greenfield projects where you actually own the architecture decisions instead of following 47 different internal guidelines.

how long you been working total?
I have 4+ years of experience in tech

4+ years... solid foundation, past that junior phase but still hungry to learn. that amazon-to-bp move makes even more sense now - you're at the perfect stage to own bigger pieces instead of being another cog.

what kind of role you looking for next?
Backend sde 2

backend sde 2... makes sense. you've got the amazon pedigree plus the bp greenfield experience. that's a killer combo for mid-level backend roles. companies love that mix of scale knowledge + scrappy building.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
Open to remote and pune hyderabad and banglore
4+ years backend + remote/bangalore/pune/hyderabad + sde 2 level... sound right?
Yes
